Calories in Indian foods, by the 100 grams.

A calm, source-linked starting point for everyday foods. Compare a few familiar entries, then adjust for the food and portion on your own plate.

Values from selected USDA FoodData Central records · Reviewed November 16, 2026

kcal
/ 100 g

A sample, not a universal calorie chart.

In the selected USDA records below, 100 g of plain idli is listed at 128 kcal, plain dosa at 210 kcal, and cooked white rice at 129 kcal. The idli record lists one item as 38 g, which calculates to about 49 kcal for that record. Actual size and recipe change the estimate.

Compare by weight.

Each name links to its USDA FoodData Central record. “Per 100 g” is a normalized reference amount, not a suggested serving.

Find the closest food record.

Search the same 13,649 USDA FoodData Central records included in QikCal. A total of 13,598 records include energy; others stay visible with energy marked unavailable. Choose the closest source record, then use its listed serving or enter your portion in grams. Recipe and preparation can change the value.

    — kcalChoose a USDA food record to calculate a portion estimate.

    Formula: source kcal per 100 g × grams ÷ 100, rounded to the nearest whole kcal. This is a reference estimate, not a measurement of your recipe.

    The recipe and the portion matter.

    One name can cover many recipes. Dal, dosa, and sambar vary with ingredients, oil, water, and cooking method. Match the closest available record, and treat it as an estimate.

    100 g is a comparison unit. It does not mean a typical idli, bowl, cup, or restaurant serving weighs 100 g. Weigh your own portion when you need a closer calculation.

    Food records have limits. Entries may be missing or use different descriptions and data periods. Open each source record to review its details and nutrient basis.

    This guide is general food information, not medical or nutrition advice. It does not set a calorie goal or recommend a diet.

    Keep the food. Add your portion.
